sections.title: What this survey contributes
sections.text: A historical map of moonshine connecting finite groups, modular functions, vertex algebras and mathematical physics. It prioritizes breadth and references over complete derivations.

sections.title: The main conceptual distinction
sections.text: A graded dimension records sizes; a graded character records how group elements act. The latter produces McKay–Thompson series and carries the stronger genus-zero claim.

sections.title: How the explanation is organized
sections.text: The survey moves from numerical clues and precise conjectures to the Moonshine module, the associated Lie algebra, denominator identities and modular equations.

sections.title: What the proof discussion clarifies
sections.text: Recurrence and modular-equation arguments explain how algebraic structure constrains entire series. The survey also distinguishes proving the identity from finding a satisfying conceptual explanation.

sections.title: A concrete correction while reading
sections.text: Equation 2.1 prints 2^45 in the Monster order. ATLAS gives 2^46; use that corrected factorization. The discrepancy is visible in the PDF and is not merely text-extraction loss.

sections.title: How to use it
sections.text: Use the section references to identify prerequisite subjects and primary proofs. Do not treat its historical conjecture statements as a current open-problem list.
